thread:
jess: Heads-up — since the kernel upgrade last night we've seen a burst of ECC/Xid alerts from eu-west1 GPUs. Looks noisy, but a few nodes hit drain thresholds.
infra-bot: ALERT: gpu_ecc_xid_rate{region=\"eu-west1\", device=\"card-3\"} = 18 spikes in 1m
noah: Can you paste the raw DCGM exporter series? want to see if it's really sustained or a single flurry.
jess: here are the two series for card-3 last 10m:
```
# from prometheus
rate(dcgm_ecc_errors_total{device=\"card-3\"}[1m])
rate(dcgm_xid_errors_total{device=\"card-3\"}[1m])
```
They spike for ~90s then drop. Prom rule fired immediately and triggered drain automation.
ashley: That's the usual: transient flares post-kernel touch. We should avoid immediate drain on single short spikes.
ashley: Proposal: move to a "metric fusion" rule that requires both: sustained ECC/Xid rate OR ECC + high SM error correlate OR for: 5m. Example rule draft:
```
- alert: GPU_Degraded_Fused
  expr: (
    increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 5 and
    increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) > 2
  ) or (
    increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[10m]) > 3 and
    max_over_time(node_gpu_sm_retire_count[10m]) > 0
  )
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Fused GPU degradation detected on {{ $labels.instance }} {{ $labels.device }}"
```
noah: +1 to fusion. Also add `card_fingerprint` label from the exporter so we can coalesce across the same physical card even if device name changes after reboot.
jess: exporter already emits `card_fingerprint` for us, good call.
miguel: we should also add an alertmanager inhibition/silence rule for nodes annotated `gpu-scheduled-rma=true` to avoid noisy paging during scheduled work. e.g. `kubectl annotate node <node> gpu-scheduled-rma=true` and a small automation to set a 24h suppression.
ashley: And change drain automation: require "fused" alert of severity=page + sustained `for: 10m`, OR explicit manual ack. No automatic drain for single-card transient spikes. We lose too much capacity with knee-jerk drains.
jess: Agreed. FYI rough numbers: recent month we had ~14 auto-drains triggered by single 60s spikes — estimated 2.2% effective GPU capacity churn and extra pod reschedules.
noah: Could we add a short-term local suppression window in exporter where it buffers and emits a debounced counter? Might reduce prometheus churn but be careful about losing signal.
ashley: I prefer keeping raw signals and handling in Prometheus/Alertmanager so we can tweak rules without touching exporter. But small exporter-side de-dup (merge identical duplicates within 10s) is ok.
miguel: I'll add an entry to oncall runbook with steps:
- Check `dcgm` graphs for device and `card_fingerprint`
- If fused alert fired, check `node_gpu_sm_retire_count` & temp
- If only 1m transient spike -> acknowledge and monitor
- If sustained 10m -> cordon+drain + RMA workflow
ashley: Also create a pager severity mapping: `page` only for fused sustained alerts, `ticket` for short/one-off Xid spikes.
jess: Can someone PR the prometheus rule and alertmanager inhibition by EOD? I'll test in staging with simulated spikes.
noah: I'll take the prometheus rule PR. I'll include `for: 10m` and `card_fingerprint` relabeling in the recording rules.
miguel: I'll add the node annotation automation and update the runbook.
ashley: I'll update drain automation to require alert label `fused=true` before action. Also add a safety that prevents auto-drain if cluster free GPU capacity < 10% to avoid capacity collapse.
jess: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll post follow-up with staging test logs.
noah: sounds good. :thumbsup:
